content:
🚨Many entrepreneurs believe that once the Certificate of Incorporation is issued, their work is complete. In reality, a few small mistakes at the beginning can become expensive legal problems later.

1️⃣Incorrect DIN Allotment:

The Director Identification Number (DIN) is linked to every company director. If the wrong person is appointed, incorrect details are submitted, or DIN-related compliances are ignored, changing the records later can be time-consuming and may delay important business decisions.

2️⃣Ignoring Post-Incorporation Compliances:

Incorporation is only the first step. Opening statutory registers, filing mandatory ROC forms, appointing auditors, and completing other legal compliances on time are equally important. Missing these requirements can result in penalties and damage the company's credibility.

3️⃣Not Opening a Current Account in the Company's Name:

Many founders continue using their personal bank account after incorporation. This mixes personal and business transactions, creates accounting issues, and raises concerns during audits, tax filings, and investor due diligence. A separate current account helps maintain transparency and financial discipline from day one.

A company is built not just by registration, but by following the right legal and financial practices from the very beginning.
comment: Another overlooked area is shareholder agreements and internal governance. Early clarity on roles, decision rights, and ownership expectations can prevent disputes that no incorporation document can solve later.
